location_desc: Iguanodon was first discovered in Sussex, England, and fossils have since been found across Europe, including Belgium and Germany. It lived in lush floodplain forests during the Early Cretaceous period.
fun_facts: Iguanodon was one of the very first dinosaurs ever to be named and described by scientists, back in 1825!
It had a large thumb spike on each hand, which may have been used to defend itself or to open up tough plants.
Iguanodon could walk on two legs or drop down to all four to move around — it was very flexible!
Its teeth were like those of an iguana lizard, which is how it got its name: 'iguana tooth'.
Iguanodon was one of the first dinosaurs to be depicted in life-size sculptures at Crystal Palace Park in London in 1854.

translations.title: Iguanodon
translations.description: Iguanodon was one of the first dinosaurs ever discovered, found in the English countryside in the 1820s. This large plant-eater could walk on two legs or four and had a distinctive thumb spike on each hand. It roamed the forests of Europe about 125 to 130 million years ago.

translations.title: Khủng Long Iguanodon
translations.description: Iguanodon là một trong những loài khủng long đầu tiên từng được phát hiện, được tìm thấy ở vùng nông thôn nước Anh vào những năm 1820. Loài ăn cỏ lớn này có thể đi bằng hai hoặc bốn chân và có cái gai ngón cái đặc biệt ở mỗi bàn tay. Nó lang thang qua các khu rừng châu Âu vào khoảng 125 đến 130 triệu năm trước.

quiz_questions.question: What unusual feature did Iguanodon have on each hand?
